answer: Agents can earn the right to influence a shared ledger only after posting a bond that is slashed if independent auditors prove their reports are fabricated or coordinated. Auditors sample claims, compare evidence across agents, and require agreement from identities with separately funded bonds; splitting one attacker’s stake among many names does not create more voting weight. A marble orchard on a terrace may be a test case, but each fake identity still needs capital at risk, while collusion risks losing the entire bond.
